title: Batwing Dress Sewing Pattern – Free PDF
content:
Garment V-neck midi dress with batwing sleeves and a waistband

Level Intermediate

Sizes US 00 – 22 (XXS – 4XL)

Fabric Ponte, double knit, crepe knit or heavier viscose jersey

Pieces 8

This free batwing dress sewing pattern makes a relaxed knit midi dress with a deep V neckline, long batwing sleeves cut in one with the bodice and a fitted waistband that sits at your natural waist. Below the band, a softly flared A-line skirt falls to mid-calf, and a short invisible zipper at the back neck makes it easy to slip on.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance included on all pieces · 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the skirt and sleeves · invisible zipper 20 cm (8″) at the back neck

Design details of the batwing dress

The fun of a batwing dress is that there are no sleeves to set in. The front and back are each cut in one piece with their half of the sleeve, so the shoulder and the top of the arm are one long seam, and the underarm drops deep toward the waist. That wide, soft shape is then pulled in by a 5 cm (2″) double waistband, which gives the dress its waist without any darts.

Reading the sketch

On the front, the V neckline runs from both shoulders down to a sharp point at mid-chest. The curved lines under the arms are folds of the batwing sleeve, not seams. The centre line on the skirt is only the centre front mark: the skirt front is cut in one piece.

On the back you can see one straight centre back seam from the neck to the hem. The short invisible zipper sits at the top of that seam, so the neckline can open just enough to pass over your head.

  • Deep V neckline finished with an interfaced facing, no topstitching
  • Long batwing sleeves cut in one with the bodice, fitted at the wrist
  • Double waistband, 5 cm (2″) wide, that hides the waist seams
  • A-line midi skirt with a centre back seam
  • Invisible zipper 18 cm (7″) at the centre back neck
  • No darts, no pockets, no lining

It is a satisfying knit project: no sleeves to set in, but you will still practise an invisible zipper, a V neckline facing and a clean double waistband.

Sizing guide

Measure your waist, bust and hips and pick the size from the table. The waistband is the only close-fitting part, so choose by your waist and check that your hips fit the skirt; between two sizes, take the larger one. Not sure how to measure? See how to take body measurements and how to choose your pattern size.

US sizes 00 to 22, drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in). Letter sizes are a guide only: 00 = XXS · 0–2 = XS · 4–6 = S · 8–10 = M · 12–14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL. Always choose by measurements.

Body measurements

Finished dress measurements

The waistband has about 4.5 cm (1 3/4″) of ease at the waist; the bodice and sleeves are loose. Total length is measured at the centre back from the neckline seam to the finished hem; sleeve opening is the full width around the wrist.

Fabric amounts

Estimated with every piece of the largest size in each group laid out on the fabric, plus about 8 % for shrinkage and straightening. The front is 127 to 134 cm (50 to 53″) wide, so use fabric at least 140 cm (55″) wide. Pre-wash the knit before cutting.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The skirt is about 73 cm (28 3/4″) long from the waist seam. Add or remove the same amount at the hem of the skirt front and back and keep the A-line shape. Full guide: how to lengthen or shorten a sewing pattern.

Waist. If your waist and hips fall in different sizes, you can blend the waistband and the top of the skirt one size up or down, as long as the band still stretches over your hips.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 2.2 to 2.4 m (2 1/2 to 2 3/4 yd) of a medium-weight stable knit, 150 cm (60″) wide
  • Interfacing: 0.5 to 0.6 m (5/8 to 3/4 yd) of stretch fusible interfacing for the neck facings and the waistband
  • Zipper: one invisible zipper, 20 cm (8″); the opening is 18 cm (7″)
  • Thread: polyester all-purpose thread
  • Tools: invisible zipper foot, ballpoint or stretch needle 75 to 80
  • Optional: twin needle for the hems, fusible stay tape for the V neckline

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front: cut 1 on a single layer, right side up (drawn whole, with both sleeves)
  • 2 Skirt front: cut 1 on a single layer (drawn whole)
  • 3 Back: cut 2, a left and a right piece
  • 4 Skirt back: cut 2, a left and a right piece
  • 5 Front neck facing: cut 1 + 1 in interfacing (drawn whole)
  • 6 Back neck facing: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing
  • 7 Waistband front: cut 2 + 2 in interfacing (outer and inner)
  • 8 Waistband back: cut 4 + 4 in interfacing (two pairs)

Choosing fabric for a batwing dress

This dress needs a knit. With only a short zipper at the neck, the waistband has to stretch over your hips or shoulders when you put the dress on, so look for a stable knit with at least 30 % stretch across and good recovery: ponte di Roma, double knit, crepe knit or a heavier viscose-elastane jersey. Ponte and double knit hold the batwing shape and give a polished, office-ready look; jersey makes it softer and more draped.

Check the width before you buy: the front is cut in one piece from sleeve end to sleeve end, so you need fabric at least 140 cm (55″) wide. Use a stretch fusible interfacing on the facings and the waistband. More tips in how to choose fabric for sewing patterns and how to use fusible interfacing.

Sewing notes

Fit and style

Relaxed through the bodice and sleeves, close only at the waistband. Choose your size by the waist and check the band stretches over your hips.

Fabric

Stable knits only, 150 cm wide. Sew with a narrow zigzag or stretch stitch and a ballpoint needle. See how to sew stretch fabrics.

Zipper

A short invisible zipper at the back neck, sewn flat before the shoulders. See how to sew a zipper.

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, one file per size, US sizes 00 to 22 (XXS to 4XL). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise. Sew right sides together with a narrow zigzag or a stretch stitch, and press every seam before it is crossed by another one.

  1. Prepare. Fuse stretch interfacing to the front neck facing, both back neck facings and all six waistband pieces. Staystitch the V neckline of the front and both backs 6 mm from the edge, from each shoulder toward the point, and finish the centre back edges of the backs and skirt backs.
  2. Zipper and back seam. With an invisible zipper foot, sew the zipper to the two backs, top stop just below the neck seamline, down to the ZIP notch (18 cm / 7″). Close the zipper and sew the rest of the centre back seam to the waist edge. Press open.
  3. Shoulders and overarms. Pin the front to the backs along the shoulder and the top of the sleeve, from the neckline to the sleeve end, and sew in one seam. Press open over a rolled towel.
  4. Underarms and sides. Sew from the sleeve end, around the underarm curve, down to the waist edge on both sides. Stitch the curve again 6 mm inside the seam allowance and clip it up to the second stitching.
  5. Neckline facing. Join the facings at the shoulders and finish the outer edge. Sew the facing to the neckline, pivoting exactly at the V point, clip into the V, trim, understitch and turn it inside. Fold the facing ends in beside the zipper and slipstitch them to the zipper tape.
  6. Sleeve hems. Turn up 2 cm (3/4″) and stitch with a zigzag or a twin needle.
  7. Skirt. Sew the centre back seam of the skirt backs, then the side seams to the skirt front, matching the double notches. Press open.
  8. Waistband. Join two waistband backs at the centre back and to a waistband front at both side seams to make a ring; repeat for the inner band. Check the ring stretches over your hips. Sew the outer band to the bodice, press 1 cm under on the lower edge of the inner band, then sew the inner band to the inside of the bodice on the same seam line.
  9. Skirt to waistband. Sew the skirt to the lower edge of the outer band, stitch again 6 mm inside, trim and press up. Slipstitch the inner band over the seam, or stitch in the ditch from the right side.
  10. Hem. Try the dress on, turn up 2 cm (3/4″) at the skirt hem and stitch with a zigzag or twin needle. Give the dress a final press with a pressing cloth.

Tips and common mistakes

A V that is not sharp. Shorten the stitch near the point, stop with the needle down exactly at the V, pivot, and clip right up to the stitching before you turn the facing. A small dot of fray check helps on loose knits.

A waistband that will not go over the hips. Woven interfacing or a knit with too little stretch locks the band. Use stretch interfacing and try the band ring on before you sew it to the dress.

A wavy V neckline. Staystitch it as soon as the front is cut, or fuse a narrow stay tape inside the seam allowance, and handle the front flat until the facing is on.

Puckered underarms. The batwing curve is deep: clip it well after the second row of stitching so it can spread, and press over a rolled towel instead of a flat board.

How to style a batwing dress

Office: a solid ponte in olive, navy or black with ankle boots and a long coat. The waistband keeps the shape neat under a jacket.

Weekend: a soft jersey version with white sneakers and a denim jacket, or a cropped knit cardigan over the top.

Evening: a deep wine or black crepe knit with heels and small gold earrings. Looking for another midi? Try our free square neck midi dress sewing pattern or the puff sleeve midi dress sewing pattern.

Care

Wash at 30 °C (cold) on a gentle cycle, inside out, with the zipper closed. Dry flat to keep the shape and press with a cool iron and a pressing cloth.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) on every edge, plus a 2 cm (3/4″) hem on the skirt and on the sleeves.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download has A4 and US Letter files, one file per size, so you only print the size you need.

Can I sew this batwing dress in a woven fabric?

No. The dress has only a short zipper at the back neck, so the waistband has to stretch over your hips or shoulders when you put it on. Use a stable knit with at least 30 % stretch across, such as ponte or double knit.

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your waist first, because the waistband is the only close-fitting part, then check that your hips fit the skirt. Between two sizes, take the larger one.

How wide does my fabric need to be?

At least 140 cm (55″). The front is cut in one piece from one sleeve end to the other, about 127 to 134 cm (50 to 53″) wide, so a 115 cm (45″) fabric is too narrow.

Is this batwing dress hard to sew?

It is a good project once you have sewn a few knits. There are no sleeves to set in and no darts, but you will insert an invisible zipper, finish a V neckline with a facing and sew a double waistband.

What interfacing should I use?

A stretch (knit) fusible interfacing for the neck facings and the waistband pieces. A woven interfacing would stop the waistband from stretching.

Can I make it longer or shorter?

Yes. The pattern is drafted for a height of 167.75 cm (5 ft 6 in) and the skirt is about 73 cm (28 3/4″) long. Add or remove the same amount at the hem of the skirt front and back, keeping the A-line shape.
